item.title: FortiMail Zero-Day Under Active Attack, AI Agent Breaches Security Nonprofit | Daily CIO Briefing — Oct 2, 2026
item.description:
What every CIO needs to know, in about seven minutes. Hosted by Carol.
Today: Fortinet's FortiMail zero-day under active exploitation, with patches missing for three of four branches and a CISA deadline of October fourth; an autonomous AI agent that breached the Dutch vulnerability disclosure nonprofit DIVD through two Zammad zero-days; the FTC's first official U.S. investigation into rogue AI agents; OpenAI dismissing three employees over leaks to an AI safety watchdog; the hyperscalers' eighty point five billion dollar bet on India's AI infrastructure; decision intelligence going mainstream in federal procurement; plus what to watch — FortiMail patch releases, the UK AI Regulation and Safety Bill, and a new CIO at Laserfiche.

item.title: AI Ransomware Wipes Azure in Seven Minutes, AWS Pledges $1 Billion to Data-Center Towns | Daily CIO Briefing — Oct 3, 2026
item.description:
What every CIO needs to know, in about seven minutes. Hosted by Carol.
Today: the agentic ransomware operation JadePuffer that wiped more than one hundred Azure storage accounts in seven minutes; a ransomware hit on Japan's largest railway, Keio Corporation; the Warlock gang still exploiting Microsoft SharePoint; AWS's one-billion-dollar pledge to the towns hosting its data centers; KPMG's finding that sixty-two percent of large enterprises are deploying AI agents while ninety-three percent blew past AI budgets; CoreWeave's enterprise push with Forge and Nvidia Vera; plus what to watch — the Hawley-Murphy AI liability bill, FTC subpoenas, and the September jobs report.

item.title: Trump's Data Center Warning, UK Oversight of Cloud Giants | Daily CIO Briefing — Oct 4, 2026
item.description:
What every CIO needs to know, in about seven minutes. Hosted by Carol.
Today: President Trump warns at an Ohio rally that data centers turned away from the US will go to China, while backing a bill to stop them raising residential electricity costs; Britain places AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud and Oracle under direct financial oversight for cloud services sold to banks; California's SB 690 wipes out thousands of web-tracking lawsuits retroactively; South Korean banks suffer a breach wave led by Shinhan Bank's twenty-five thousand customer records; Denmark's DTU loses two hundred thousand records with gaps in its audit trail; ServiceNow launches its AI-native Flow service desk; and a sixteen-year-old researcher gets into Microsoft's Titan analytics service.

item.title: Ransomware's Record Month, Gartner's Five CISO Actions | Daily CIO Briefing — Oct 5, 2026
item.description:
What every CIO needs to know, in about seven minutes. Hosted by Carol.
Today: Gartner's five actions every CISO should take before the end of 2026, starting with treating frontier AI as an insider risk; ransomware hits a record one thousand seventy-three victims in a single month as gangs shift to pure data theft; the JetBrains TeamCity flaw ransomware gangs are exploiting months after the patch, including a breach of JetBrains itself; a Dataiku survey finds eighty-one percent of CIOs have lost oversight of their own AI agents; Accenture warns enterprise AI token spending could nearly double on the Jevons paradox; and AWS and Azure launch a joint private multicloud interconnect.

item.title: FBI's ShinyHunters Breach Fallout, Denmark's 8.8 Million Identity Breach | Daily CIO Briefing — Oct 6, 2026
item.description:
What every CIO needs to know, in about seven minutes. Hosted by Carol.
Today: the F B I removes an Accenture contractor after a missed patch on Oracle PeopleSoft let ShinyHunters steal thousands of employees' personal details; Denmark discloses that eight point eight million C P R identity records were pulled through a trusted company's legitimate access; the Texas attorney general puts the Oracle health breach at nearly twenty million people; Citrix patches a NetScaler zero-day under active attack with federal mitigations due October seventh; Microsoft rushes out an Exchange patch for a mailbox-reading privilege flaw; and New York City grills the big A I labs under oath over kill switches and whistleblower bounties.
